title: Workload discovery regions, per-region status, and turning data collection off

prose.label: Selecting regions.
prose.text: {{select-regions}} {{help-region-list}} The API lists the regions discovery supports: [[cloud-connector.regions:wds-endpoint]], with each entry's fields in [[cloud-connector.regions:wds-cloud-types]]; whether that set matches the Zero Trust Gateway and Cloud Connector lists is open: [[cloud-connector.regions:region-set-parity]]. {{regions-by-id}} {{update-carries-regions}}

prose.label: Per-region status.
prose.text: {{status-strings}} {{region-status-boolean}} How the console's strings relate to the boolean is unresolved {{gap:region-status-representation}}. {{private-ip-count}} The duplicate IP counter is covered with namespaces: [[cloud-connector.workload-discovery.namespaces:duplicate-ip-one-shown]].

prose.label: Turning data collection off.
prose.text: {{data-collection-toggle}} {{change-state-api}} What happens to tags already delivered while collection is off is not stated {{gap:disabled-tag-retention}}.

prose.label: Toggling from the SDKs.
prose.text: The Go function for this call fails on every call: [[cloud-connector.sdk-go.service-defects:public-cloud-change-state-nil-payload]]. {{python-change-state-body}} {{python-enable-not-query}}

checks.do: Whether every region that holds the workloads is selected on the account.
The Discovery Service Status of the region on the account details page, and whether data collection was disabled for the account.
When toggling data collection by API, send `enable` as a query parameter directly rather than through the Go or Python helper.

select-regions.statement: Regions where workloads are deployed are selected when the account is added; if a region where workloads run is not selected, the discovery service does not discover those workloads and tag-based security policies are not applied to them.

quotes: In the Region section, select one or more regions where your workloads are deployed.

If you do not select one or more regions where you have workloads deployed, the Zscaler discovery service does not discover the workloads, and tag-based security policies are not applied to the workloads.

regions-by-id.statement: Clients select regions by ID: the Terraform resource's `supported_regions` is a set of IDs, and the Python SDK takes `supported_region_ids` and sends them as `supportedRegions`.

quotes: "supported_regions": setIDsSchemaTypeCustom(nil, "Regions supported by Zscaler’s Tag Discovery Service."),
supported_region_ids (list): List of IDs for supported region objects.
("supported_region_ids", "supportedRegions"),

update-carries-regions.statement: The account update request carries `supportedRegions`, as the create request does.

status-strings.statement: The account details page shows a Discovery Service Status per region; the most commonly displayed values are Success (running as expected), Disabled (re-enable data collection from the AWS Accounts page), Error (the service has discovered an issue) and Starting Discovery (data collection has not been started).

quotes: Discovery Service Status: The status of the discovery service. The following statuses are the most commonly displayed:
Success: The service is running as expected.
Disabled: The service is disabled. To re-enable data collection, go to the AWS Accounts page.
Error: The service has discovered an issue.
Starting Discovery: Data collection has not been started.

region-status-boolean.statement: In the API contract and the Go SDK, each entry of the account's `regionStatus` has a boolean `status` described as the operational status of the region.

expect.description: Indicates the operational status of the region.

quotes: // Indicates the operational status of the region. Status bool `json:"status,omitempty"`

private-ip-count.statement: No of Private IP Addresses counts the workloads the discovery service found, one per IP address, so a workload with several IP addresses is shown as several workloads.

quotes: No of Private IP Addresses: The number of workloads that the tag discovery service has discovered. Each IP address represents a workload. If a workload has multiple IP addresses within it, it is shown as multiple workloads.

data-collection-toggle.statement: An account's menu offers Disable Data Collection, which stops the tag discovery process, and Enable Data Collection, which starts it.

quotes: Disable Data Collection: Zscaler stops the tag discovery process.
Enable Data Collection: Zscaler begins the tag discovery process.

change-state-api.statement: The API enables or disables an AWS account in all regions with a PUT on the account's change-state path, taking a boolean `enable` query parameter (true enables, false disables).

expect.description: Enables or disables a specific AWS account in all regions based on the provided ID.

python-change-state-body.statement: The Python SDK's `change_state_public_cloud_info` documents `query_params.enable`, but it copies its keyword arguments into the request body and builds the request without query parameters.

quotes: ``[query_params.enable]`` {bool}: Set true to enable the AWS account, and false to disable it.
body = {} body.update(kwargs) request, error = self._request_executor.create_request(http_method, api_url, body, {}, {})

python-enable-not-query.statement: A Python call that passes `query_params={"enable": ...}` therefore sends it inside the JSON body, not as the `enable` query parameter the API reads.
python-enable-not-query.conditions: Follows from the method's code; the request executor's body handling was not traced further and the call was not observed on the wire.

help-region-list.statement: The account details help says the supported AWS regions include us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-1, us-west-2, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, ap-southeast-1, ap-south-1 and ap-southeast-2.

region-status-representation.title: How the console's region status strings map to the boolean API status
region-status-representation.detail: The account details help shows Success, Disabled, Error and Starting Discovery as the most common region statuses, while the API contract and Go SDK type `regionStatus[].status` as a boolean. Whether the API returns a richer value than documented, or the console derives the strings from the boolean plus other fields, is not shown, so a region row read through the API cannot be mapped to a console status.
region-status-representation.blocks: Reporting a region's discovery status from API or SDK reads.

disabled-tag-retention.title: Tags already delivered after data collection is disabled
disabled-tag-retention.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Disabling stops tag discovery; policy that referenced discovered tags loses its workload-identity binding for that account until re-enabled.' The help says only that disabling stops the tag discovery process; whether Cloud Connectors keep or drop the tag mappings they already hold is not stated.
disabled-tag-retention.blocks: Predicting tag-based policy matches while an account's data collection is disabled.
